summary: Wiley Lavender Maknoor is a small New Jersey partnership at 216 Amboy Ave in Metuchen practicing matrimonial, civil litigation, real estate/zoning, business and estate law, with two named attorneys on its site. The firm markets itself on volume (200+ cases per year, 1K+ clients) and on partner-level responsiveness, but its only intake channels are a phone line staffed 9-5 weekdays and a Webflow contact form with no online scheduling. Its 2025 Webflow relaunch still carries template leftovers (placeholder city text, example.com mailto links) and a single blog post, suggesting marketing and intake operations are handled lightly by the partners themselves.

facts.fact: Office address is 216 Amboy Ave, Metuchen, NJ 08840; main phone (732) 494-6099; phone hours listed as Mon-Fri 9AM to 5PM.

Practice areas offered in the site's contact-form service menu: Matrimonial, Personal injury, Estate Planning & Administration, Business & Corporate, Real Estate/Zoning and Land Use, Liquor licenses, Litigation.
Home page advertises 50+ years of experience, 200+ successful cases per year, 95% client satisfaction rate and 1K+ clients across New Jersey; the Our History page states 5K+ clients instead.
Our History page repeats the 50+/200+/95% metrics but says '5K+ Clients across New Jersey', inconsistent with the 1K+ figure on the home page.
The attorneys page lists two attorney profiles, Larry Lavender and Pankaj Maknoor, and the site describes clients working 'directly with our partners' with 'no handoffs'.
Larry Lavender's bio: Rutgers JD/MBA, 20+ years in practice, co-founded the firm after defending insurers in multimillion-dollar premises-liability and product-defect cases.
Pankaj Maknoor's bio: civil and commercial litigation, landlord/tenant disputes, consumer fraud, quiet title actions, personal injury, debt collection and Chapter 7 bankruptcy.
Consultations are booked 'by calling our office or filling out the contact form on our website'; no online calendar or self-scheduling tool is offered.
Blog index contains a single article, 'High-Asset Divorce in New Jersey: Your Top 5 Questions Answered', dated Dec 22, 2025.
The Q&A page references a 'Pricing' page and lists IP and contract-drafting services that do not appear in the site's services menu or practice-area pages.
Footer links to a Facebook page (facebook.com/WLMLawFirm) and a LinkedIn company page (linkedin.com/company/wiley-lavender-maknoor-p-c).
Site is built on Webflow and was last published Dec 22, 2025; every page loads Google Tag Manager (GTM-ML8VXZ7C) and a Google Analytics 4 tag (G-8WYZ2PDNST).
There is no careers page (wileylavender.com/careers returns HTTP 404) and SimplyHired returned zero job listings for the firm name.

operations_signals: Intake is two-channel only: phone (732) 494-6099 during Mon-Fri 9AM-5PM, or a website form; the site explicitly says consultations are scheduled by calling or submitting the form (https://www.wileylavender.com/our-attorneys).

Contact form is a Webflow form with required first/last name, phone, email, a required practice-area dropdown (7 options) and a message box, Cloudflare Turnstile bot protection, and a redirect to a /thank-you page; submissions appear to land in email with no case-management routing visible (https://www.wileylavender.com/contact-us).

The forms and bios publish individual partner emails (larry@, Pankaj@wileylavender.com), so inquiries are triaged by partners rather than a central intake desk (https://www.wileylavender.com/attorney-details/pankaj-maknoor).
No published after-hours coverage; phone hours are limited to weekday business hours and no emergency or 24/7 line is mentioned (https://www.wileylavender.com/contact-us).

Practice mix skews to deadline-driven, document-heavy matters: divorce/custody/support, landlord-tenant, consumer fraud, quiet title, debt collection, Chapter 7 bankruptcy and real estate closings (https://www.wileylavender.com/services/matrimonial).
Service area is statewide New Jersey with a single Metuchen office; no branch locations are listed (https://www.wileylavender.com/contact-us).
Firm publishes volume metrics (200+ cases per year, 1K+ clients) implying high per-matter intake and document throughput relative to a two-attorney roster (https://www.wileylavender.com/).
hiring_signals: No careers or join-us page exists on the site (/careers returns HTTP 404) (https://www.wileylavender.com/careers).
SimplyHired search for the firm name returned zero listings, and a variant name search also returned zero (https://www.simplyhired.com/search?q=%22Lavender+Maknoor%22).

Indeed, LinkedIn Jobs and ZipRecruiter pages for the firm could not be retrieved (403 bot blocks), so absence of postings is only confirmed on SimplyHired (https://www.indeed.com/cmp/Wiley-Lavender-Maknoor/jobs).
The site emphasizes that clients work directly with partners and that there are 'no handoffs', which is consistent with a thin support staff (https://www.wileylavender.com/our-attorneys).
review_themes: Only self-published testimonials were retrievable: two quotes on the home page praise responsiveness, transparent fees and direct partner access; these are firm-curated, not independent reviews (https://www.wileylavender.com/).

The site's stated core values are responsiveness, transparency and personal partnership, which reads as a response to client anxiety about slow replies and surprise fees rather than as evidence of past complaints (https://www.wileylavender.com/).

Independent review sources (Google Business Profile, Yelp, BBB, Avvo, Super Lawyers) were blocked or returned no readable results during this research, so no third-party rating or complaint theme could be verified (https://www.yelp.com/biz/wiley-lavender-maknoor-metuchen).
tech_footprint: Website is a Webflow build (site ID 683f5c68a870f40a5e542f4a) last published Dec 22, 2025, with Google Tag Manager and GA4 analytics installed (https://www.wileylavender.com/).

Contact form is a native Webflow form secured by Cloudflare Turnstile; no Clio, Lawmatics, HubSpot, Calendly or other CRM/booking widget is loaded on the pages reviewed (https://www.wileylavender.com/contact-us).
No client portal, document upload or payment link is advertised; the only self-service path is the message form (https://www.wileylavender.com/contact-us).

Template leftovers remain live: the mobile nav shows placeholder text 'SAN FRANCISCO - 18:24PM', and attorney bio mailto links still point to info@example.com while displaying the real address (https://www.wileylavender.com/attorney-details/larry-lavender).
Content publishing is minimal: one blog post dated Dec 22, 2025, on a high-asset divorce topic (https://www.wileylavender.com/blog).
Marketing surface is limited to the website plus a Facebook page and LinkedIn company page linked in the footer (https://www.wileylavender.com/contact-us).
growth_signals: The site was rebuilt on Webflow and republished in December 2025 with new branding assets, indicating a recent marketing refresh (https://www.wileylavender.com/).

The firm advertises statewide reach ('1K+ clients across New Jersey', attorneys licensed in multiple states) while operating from one Metuchen office, pointing to geographic expansion without added locations (https://www.wileylavender.com/our-history).
Added service lines beyond the litigation core, including liquor licenses, estate planning and business formation, appear in the site's service menu (https://www.wileylavender.com/contact-us).

No expansion, award or acquisition news could be verified; a Google News RSS query for the firm name returned no clearly attributable coverage (https://news.google.com/rss/search?q=%22Wiley+Lavender+Maknoor%22).
decision_maker: Larry Lavender, co-founder/partner (listed on the firm's Our Attorneys page and bio; the site does not state formal titles) — https://www.wileylavender.com/attorney-details/larry-lavender. Pankaj Maknoor is the second named partner — https://www.wileylavender.com/attorney-details/pankaj-maknoor

inferences.inference: Inquiries that arrive outside 9-5 weekdays, or while partners are in court, likely wait until the next business day; there is no after-hours capture beyond a web form.
inferences.reasoning: The site lists only weekday 9-5 phone hours and a form, with no answering service, chat, or online scheduling mentioned anywhere on the contact or attorney pages.

inferences.inference: A meaningful share of partner time is consumed by repetitive intake qualification, document drafting and docket follow-up rather than strategy.
inferences.reasoning: Two named attorneys report 200+ cases per year across matrimonial, landlord-tenant, debt collection, bankruptcy and real estate work, all document-heavy and deadline-driven, with no visible paralegal, intake or case-management tooling on the site or in job listings.

inferences.inference: The firm's intake funnel leaks high-intent leads because the form gives no response-time expectation, no confirmation of who will reply, and no way to self-schedule.
inferences.reasoning: The contact page offers a seven-option service dropdown and a message box but no calendar, no fee/consultation detail and no auto-acknowledgement beyond a generic thank-you page.

inferences.inference: Marketing content and site QA are deprioritized relative to billable work.
inferences.reasoning: Live pages still contain placeholder city text and info@example.com mailto links, the Q&A page references a pricing page that does not exist, and the blog has a single post.

inferences.inference: Client-experience marketing is compensating for something: the site leads with responsiveness, transparency and 'no hidden fees' as core values.
inferences.reasoning: In legal services these positioning themes typically respond to client anxieties about unanswered calls and billing surprises; the firm repeats them in values tabs and testimonials.

inferences.inference: Inconsistent client-count claims (1K+ vs 5K+) suggest metrics are copied across pages without a single source of truth.
inferences.reasoning: The home page and the Our History page present identical 50+/200+/95% figures but differ by 5x on total clients.

inferences.inference: Hiring is likely done through referrals or the state bar network rather than public job boards.
inferences.reasoning: No careers page exists and no listings surfaced on SimplyHired; a firm handling 200+ matters a year with two attorneys would normally need support staff, so recruiting may be informal or via contract paralegals.

data_gaps: Independent review content could not be retrieved: Google Business Profile, Yelp, BBB, Avvo, Justia, Martindale and Super Lawyers pages were bot-blocked (403/429/JS-only) or returned no readable results, so star ratings and complaint themes are unverified.
No confirmed job postings: Indeed, LinkedIn Jobs and ZipRecruiter were blocked; only SimplyHired could be checked (zero results).
Current headcount, staff roles (paralegal, receptionist, bookkeeper) and whether any contract staff are used are unknown.
Case management, billing and document software in use is not visible publicly; only the website stack (Webflow, GTM/GA4, Turnstile) could be confirmed.
Formal titles for the named partners (managing partner, founding partner) are not stated on the site.
No financial, revenue or case-type volume breakdown is published; the 200+ cases and client-count figures are unverified self-reported marketing claims.
No news, awards, expansion or acquisition coverage could be attributed to the firm; a Google News RSS hit mentioning the firm name could not be confirmed as relevant.
